report.summary: Reviewed chunk 5 of vet.py: defines _defang, scan_text, _scan_file, vet_skill with docstring claims.
risks: _scan_file | medium | Claims 'looks binary' check uses first 4096 bytes, but raw[:4096] may raise IndexError for small files; Python handles slices beyond length gracefully, so no bug. | Confirm that raw[:4096] is safe for files < 4096 bytes.

vet_skill | medium | Comment says 'Skipping it silently would be a hole' but the code for __pycache__ exemption is not present in this chunk. | Verify the __pycache__ exemption logic in the next chunk.
scan_text | low | Line number calculation uses binary search on starts list; if text is empty, starts = [0] and line_of(0) returns 1, which may be acceptable. | Confirm behavior for empty text.

handoff.purpose: Defines defanging, scanning, file scanning, and skill vetting functions.

symbols.name: _defang
symbols.note: Removes invisible characters from text and returns count removed.

symbols.name: scan_text
symbols.note: Scans defanged text for all rule matches, returns list of Findings.

symbols.name: _scan_file
symbols.note: Reads a file, validates it, scans it, returns findings or error string.

symbols.name: vet_skill
symbols.note: Vets a skills.Skill dataclass, returns Verdict.

claims.text: Text with invisible characters removed, and how many were removed.
Removal, not replacement: a zero-width space between ``e`` and ``val`` should make the scanner see ``eval``, which is what the interpreter and the reader both see.
claims.why: The function uses str.translate to remove characters in _INVISIBLE, not replace them.

claims.text: Positions shift, so line numbers come from the ORIGINAL text -- see ``scan_text``.
claims.why: scan_text's docstring says 'Line numbers are computed from the defanged text too', contradicting this claim.

claims.text: Every rule hit in one blob. Deterministic: rules in table order, matches in file order, so two runs over the same bytes produce identical findings.
claims.why: The function iterates RULES in order, uses regex finditer which yields matches in order, and appends to a list.

claims.text: Scanning happens on the DEFANGED text so invisible characters cannot split a keyword.
claims.why: The function calls _defang(text) and then uses the returned stripped text for regex matching.

claims.text: Line numbers are computed from the defanged text too, which can differ from the original by at most the number of stripped characters on preceding lines -- an acceptable drift, and the finding names the rule and the excerpt, so a human can still find it.
claims.why: The function uses line_of(m.start()) where line_of uses starts built from defanged text.

claims.text: Decoding with replacement would let a crafted byte sequence hide a match, so an undecodable file is unscannable, not best-effort.
claims.why: The function raises UnicodeDecodeError and returns an error string without fallback decoding.
The function is static (no self), and returns a Verdict (fail-closed by design).

claims.text: Takes the parsed dataclass rather than a path so there is exactly one ``SKILL.md`` parser in this repo — ``skills.load_skill`` — and this module cannot disagree with it about what a skill is.
claims.why: Referenced function skills.load_skill is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A ``__pycache__/x.cpython-*.pyc`` is a DERIVATIVE of an ``x.py`` we scanned, so it carries no information the scan of the source did not already cover. Skipping it silently would be a hole (bytecode can outlive or replace its source), so the exemption is conditional: the sibling source must actually be in the scanned set. A planted or orphaned .pyc still lands in `skipped` and still makes the verdict UNSCANNABLE. Without this, every skill that has ever been run sits permanently at UNSCANNABLE, and a gate that is always amber is a gate nobody reads.
claims.why: The actual logic for this exemption is not present in this chunk.

observations.what: The _defang docstring claims line numbers come from original text, but scan_text contradicts that.
vet_skill references __pycache__ exemption logic that is not in this chunk.
The 'looks binary' check uses raw[:4096]; for files smaller than 4096 bytes, this slice is safe and returns the whole file.
